title: EduTrack Pro — student grade management
short: A SaaS-style grading dashboard for schools: marks entry, automatic grading, live merit rankings and analytics — with Google Sheets as the database.
problem: Schools keep marks in spreadsheets, then rebuild the same work by hand every term: totals, percentages, grades, merit lists and report cards. The numbers already exist; what is missing is anything that turns them into an answer. Ranking 1,200 students means sorting a sheet and hoping nobody typed over a formula.
solution: A dashboard that sits on top of the school’s existing Google Sheet. Marks are entered through a validated form and the grade, percentage and rank recalculate instantly, writing straight back to the sheet. Rankings, subject analytics and the merit list are generated from live data rather than rebuilt each term.
features: Quick marks entry with grade and percentage calculated as you type
Auto-graded student records, sortable and searchable across the full roster
Dashboard overview: total students, class average, pass rate, A+ achievers
Subject-wise class averages and grade distribution
Performance trend across the academic year, compared to the previous cohort
Subject × class heatmap identifying weak areas per section
Automated insights flagging weak subjects and students needing attention
Merit list with podium view, tie-breaking by total score
Report cards and CSV / PDF export
Live two-way sync with Google Sheets
challenges: Keeping the interface responsive while every keystroke triggers a recalculation and a write back to Sheets. Marks are held in local state and reconciled with the sheet in batches, so entry never blocks on the network, and rank recalculation runs over the cached roster rather than re-reading the spreadsheet.
results: Grade, percentage and rank calculated on entry instead of at term end
Merit list and subject analytics generated from live data
The school keeps its data in its own Google account

gallery.caption: Dashboard overview — KPIs, subject averages and grade distribution
Student records and quick marks entry, auto-saved to Sheets
Performance analytics — year trend, heatmap and automated insights
Rankings — term toppers podium and the full merit list

title: Fashion jewellery online store
short: A storefront and order system for a jewellery brand selling through social media.
problem: Orders arrived through Instagram DMs and WhatsApp messages, were copied into a notebook, and were regularly lost or duplicated. There was no product catalogue customers could browse, and no reliable record of what had been shipped.
solution: A storefront with a full product catalogue, cart and checkout, backed by an admin panel where every order moves through a clear status pipeline. Stock decrements automatically on order, and each new order triggers a WhatsApp notification so nothing sits unnoticed.
features: Product catalogue with categories, variants and stock levels
Order pipeline: new → confirmed → packed → shipped → delivered
WhatsApp notification on every new order
challenges: Migrating a year of order history out of chat threads and a spreadsheet into a clean database without losing customer records, and keeping checkout usable on low-end phones with slow connections.
results: Order details captured once, at the point of sale
Stock and order status visible in one place
Checkout usable on 3G and entry-level devices

title: Inventory management web app
short: A Google Apps Script interface over an existing stock sheet used by five branch staff.
problem: Stock lived in a Google Sheet that five people edited directly. Rows were overwritten, formulas were deleted by accident, and nobody could tell who had changed a quantity or when.
solution: The sheet stayed exactly where it was; a web app went on top of it. Staff now use a form-driven interface with validation and role-based access, and every movement is written to a log with a user and timestamp.
features: Stock in / stock out entry with validation
Live stock levels with low-stock highlighting
Movement log with user and timestamp
Search and filter across thousands of rows
Data stays entirely in the client Google Sheet
challenges: Apps Script execution quotas meant naive per-row reads were far too slow over a large sheet. Batching reads and caching lookup tables brought interactions back under a second.
results: Direct sheet editing eliminated for day-to-day use
Every stock movement attributable to a person
Daily summary replaces manual end-of-day counting

title: Construction company website
short: A corporate site with a project gallery and a structured quote request flow.
problem: The firm had strong completed work and no way to show it. Enquiries came by phone with no detail, so every quote required three follow-up calls before anything could be estimated.
solution: A corporate website with a filterable project gallery and a structured quote form that captures project type, scale, location and timeline up front. Enquiries land in an admin panel with a status pipeline.
features: Project gallery filtered by type and scale
Service pages for each contracting category
Enquiry pipeline in the admin panel
challenges: Site galleries were heavy with large photographs. Responsive image sizes and lazy loading kept the gallery under a two-second load on mobile.
results: Enquiries arrive with the detail needed to quote
Completed work presented in one browsable place
Quote requests tracked rather than lost in call logs

title: School management system
short: Students, attendance, fees and results across three campuses in one system.
problem: Each campus kept its own registers and fee books. Consolidating anything for the whole school meant a week of manual collation, and fee defaulters were usually spotted a month late.
solution: A single system covering student records, daily attendance, fee vouchers and exam results, with campus-scoped roles so staff see only their own campus while administration sees everything.
features: Student records with guardian details and documents
Fee vouchers, payment tracking and defaulter lists
Exam entry, grading and printable result cards
PDF generation for vouchers and results
challenges: Migrating several years of records from inconsistent spreadsheets required a reconciliation step and a review screen before anything was committed to the live database.
results: Cross-campus reporting available on demand
Fee position visible daily instead of monthly
Result cards generated rather than typed

title: Attendance & payroll web app
short: Attendance capture and payroll calculation on top of Google Sheets.
problem: Attendance was marked on paper and typed into a spreadsheet at month end. Overtime was calculated by hand, and payroll disputes were common because nobody could reconstruct a day.
solution: A web app for daily attendance marking, with shift rules, overtime and deductions calculated automatically. Payslips generate as PDFs from the same sheet the accountant already used.
features: Shift, overtime and late rules applied automatically
challenges: Payroll rules differed by employee category. Rules were moved into a configuration sheet so the client can change rates without touching code.
results: Month-end payroll reduced from days to a single run
Overtime calculated consistently
Any past day reconstructable from the log

title: Sales analytics dashboard
short: Branch, product and trend reporting pulled into one live dashboard.
problem: Each branch emailed a spreadsheet weekly. By the time the numbers were combined they were a week old, and comparing branches or spotting a declining product line was guesswork.
solution: A dashboard reading directly from the sales database, with branch comparison, product performance, trend charts and exports. Managers see their own branch; head office sees all of them.
features: Live revenue, orders and average-order-value tiles
Date range filtering and Excel export
challenges: Aggregating several years of transactions on every page load was slow. Pre-aggregated summary tables refreshed on a schedule brought queries under 200ms.
results: Reporting lag reduced from a week to live
Branch performance comparable at a glance
Weekly spreadsheet collation eliminated

title: Photographer portfolio
short: An image-led portfolio with booking enquiries and package pages.
problem: The work lived on social media, where it was compressed, buried and impossible to organise by type. Enquiries arrived without dates, locations or budget.
solution: A portfolio site with full-resolution galleries organised by shoot type, package pages with clear inclusions, and a booking form that captures event date, venue and package interest.
features: Galleries by category with lightbox viewing
Booking enquiry form with date and venue
challenges: Large images versus load time. Responsive image sets, modern formats and progressive loading kept galleries fast without visibly degrading quality.
results: Work presented at full quality, organised by type
Enquiries include date, venue and package
Packages answer pricing questions before contact

title: Clinic appointment system
short: Online booking, doctor schedules and automated appointment reminders.
problem: Appointments were booked by phone into a paper diary. Double bookings were routine, and no-shows were high because nobody was reminded.
solution: An online booking system with per-doctor schedules and real-time slot availability, plus automatic WhatsApp and email reminders. Reception keeps a single day view of every doctor.
features: Online booking with live slot availability
Reception day view across all doctors
challenges: Concurrent bookings for the same slot. Database-level locking on slot reservation removed the race condition entirely.
results: Double bookings eliminated
Reminders sent automatically before every appointment
Reception works from one screen instead of a diary

title: Invoice generator
short: Branded PDF invoices generated from a sheet, with payment tracking.
problem: Invoices were built by duplicating a document, editing it by hand and exporting a PDF. Numbering drifted, totals were occasionally wrong, and nobody could say what was outstanding.
solution: A web app that generates branded PDF invoices from client and line-item data, with automatic sequential numbering, tax calculation and a payment status view showing exactly what is outstanding.
features: Client and line-item entry with automatic totals
challenges: Getting PDF output to match the existing brand layout precisely, including multi-page invoices with repeating headers.
results: Invoice creation reduced to a single form
Numbering and totals consistent by construction
Outstanding balances visible at any time

title: Real estate listing platform
short: Property listings with map search, saved searches and agent management.
problem: Listings were spread across classified sites and a Facebook page, each with different details. Buyers phoned to ask questions the listing should have answered.
solution: A listing platform with structured property data, map-based search, filters on every attribute that matters, and per-agent portfolios. Buyers save searches and get alerts on new matches.
features: Structured listings with full attribute set
Enquiry routing to the listing agent
challenges: Map performance with several hundred pins. Clustering and viewport-bounded queries kept panning smooth on mobile.
results: One authoritative listing per property
Buyers self-serve details previously asked by phone
Enquiries routed to the right agent automatically

title: Restaurant website with ordering
short: Menu, table reservation and direct ordering without marketplace commission.
problem: All online orders came through delivery marketplaces taking a substantial commission, and the restaurant had no direct relationship with its own customers.
solution: A website with the full menu, direct ordering for pickup and delivery, and table reservations. Orders print to the kitchen and notify staff by WhatsApp.
features: Menu with categories, options and photos
Direct ordering for pickup and delivery
challenges: Keeping menu availability in sync between branches during service, so a sold-out item disappears immediately for that location only.
results: A commission-free ordering channel
Direct customer contact details retained
Reservations and orders in one system

title: Expense tracker & reporting
short: Departmental expense capture with approval flow and budget reporting.
problem: Expenses were submitted as photographed receipts in a group chat and reconciled once a quarter, by which point nobody remembered what half of them were for.
solution: An expense system with categorised entry, receipt upload, a two-step approval flow and live budget-versus-actual reporting per department.
features: Categorised expense entry with receipt upload
challenges: Receipt images of wildly varying size. Server-side compression and thumbnailing kept storage and page loads reasonable.
results: Expenses captured at the time they occur
Approvals tracked instead of assumed
Budget position visible during the month
